questions.q: Why is a one-way ANOVA preferred over running several pairwise t-tests on three or more groups?
options: t-tests can't compare means
ANOVA always finds a significant result
ANOVA asks one overall question first, avoiding the inflated false-alarm rate of many separate tests
ANOVA works only when groups have different sizes
questions.explain: Each extra test is another chance for a Type I error. ANOVA tests 'any difference among the means?' as one hypothesis.

questions.q: What does the F statistic compare?
options: Observed and expected category counts
Between-group variability to within-group variability
The median to the mean
The sample size to the effect size
questions.explain: F is the ratio of between-group to within-group variance (each per degree of freedom). Near 1 suggests noise; large values suggest real differences.

questions.q: The ANOVA on three page designs gave F = 7.359, p = 0.0009. What can you conclude?
options: All three designs differ from one another
Design C is the best
The null that all three means are equal is implausible; a post-hoc test is needed to say which differ
There's a 99.91% chance the designs differ
questions.explain: ANOVA says at least one mean differs. It does not identify which pairs, and the p-value is not the probability that the designs differ.

questions.q: In the lesson, eta squared was about 0.077. How should it be read?
options: Page design explains roughly 7.7% of the total variability in order value
There is a 7.7% chance the result is a false alarm
The designs differ by 7.7 dollars
7.7% of visitors changed their behavior
questions.explain: Eta squared = between-group sum of squares / total sum of squares, the share of variability associated with group membership.

questions.q: In the Tukey HSD output, A vs. C had p = 0.0006 but B vs. C had p = 0.0606. What is the fair interpretation?
options: B and C are proven identical
A is proven identical to B
The post-hoc test is invalid
A and C clearly differ, while the data can't clearly separate B from its neighbors, which is not the same as proving they are equal
questions.explain: A non-significant pairwise result means insufficient evidence for a difference at this sample size, not evidence of equality.
